intro: Electric current is the rate of flow of electric charge. A battery provides the potential difference that pushes charges through a conductor, and the conductor opposes this flow with its resistance. Ohm's law connects these three quantities.
keyPoints: Current I = Q/t, measured in ampere (A). 1 A = 1 C/s.
Potential difference V = W/Q, measured in volt (V).
Ohm's law: V = IR (at constant temperature).
Resistance depends on length, area and material: R = ρL/A.
Series: same current, resistances add. Parallel: same voltage, reciprocals add.
Commercial unit of energy: 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10⁶ J.

examples.title: Charge
examples.problem: A current of 0.5 A flows through a bulb for 10 minutes. Find the charge that flows.

examples.title: Resistors in series
examples.problem: Resistors of 5 Ω, 8 Ω and 12 Ω are connected in series to a 6 V battery. Find the current.

examples.title: Resistors in parallel
examples.problem: Resistors of 5 Ω, 10 Ω and 30 Ω are connected in parallel to a 12 V battery. Find the total resistance and the current drawn.

examples.title: Cost of electricity
examples.problem: A 400 W refrigerator runs 8 hours a day. Find the cost of running it for 30 days at ₹3.00 per kWh.
